Record accepted. What it says:

**civicbeam**, six stores holding personal data:

| Store | Kind | Personal data | Erasure |
|---|---|---|---|
| `users` | relational | email, full_name, phone, created_at | `no_entry_point` |
| `documents` | relational | title, body (linked by `user_id`, models.py:27) | `no_entry_point` |
| `uploads` | S3 bucket | object key built from user id, uploaded bytes | `no_entry_point` |
| `doc_search` | Elasticsearch index | owner_email, title | `no_entry_point` |
| `events` | RabbitMQ queue | email in the message body | `no_entry_point` |
| `nightly_dump` | backup file | email, full_name, phone | `no_schedule_evidenced` |

The deciding finding: there is no account-deletion path anywhere in the repository. A search for delete/remove/purge across all Python files returns one line — `cascade="all, delete"` on `User.documents` (models.py:19) — and nothing deletes a `User`, so that cascade never fires. `storage.py`, `search.py` and `queue.py` each define a write call and no delete call. `jobs/dump.py` rewrites `nightly_dump.json` on every run with no rotation or expiry.

Retention table is empty: the code carries no number of days anywhere.

Observations recorded separately, not as findings: region `eu-central-1` (config.py:9), the Elasticsearch and RabbitMQ hosts (config.py:10–11), and `ServerSideEncryption="AES256"` on uploads (storage.py:21). `catalog.py` (plans) and `utils/text.py` were read and left out — no link to a person. Only README.md and requirements.txt went unscanned, as non-Python.

Controller, purposes, legal basis, transfers, retention justification and the recipient kind of each store are left blank for you to fill.
